what: A screen on the wall that draws one signal against another, so a sound becomes a shape: a line, a loop, a cloud or a flower.
how: The dot moves left and right with X and up and down with Y, and leaves a short glowing trail. Two sine waves of the same pitch make a circle or ellipse, a mono sound (the same on both) makes a straight diagonal line, and a wide stereo sound makes a cloud. If Y is not patched, it is the same as X. Both signals pass on to the outputs. It shows its picture even when nothing downstream is heard.

ins.x: The signal that moves the dot left and right.
ins.y: The signal that moves the dot up and down. Unpatched, it copies X.

knobs.gain: How big the picture is. Turn it up to see quiet signals, down if the picture is cut off at the edges.
knobs.turn: X-Y draws the signals as they are. L-R turns the picture a quarter turn, as a stereo scope does, so a mono sound stands straight up instead of lying diagonal.

try: Patch two VCOs (oscillators) into X and Y, set to similar pitches and nudge one slightly: the shape slowly turns inside out as the pitches drift.
